title: close
summary: Close figures or networking resources in MATLAB and RunMat.

gpu_support.notes: Networking and plotting state run on the host CPU. Numeric figure targets must already be host values and are rejected before provider dispatch when resident.

tested.integration: runmat-core close command rewrite and no-current-figure execution tests

description: `close` releases plotting figures and TCP clients/servers. Bare `close` targets the current figure and is a no-op when no figures exist, so common startup code such as `clc; clear; close` is safe. In RunMat mode, typed integer figure numbers are exact structural selectors; compatibility mode accepts ordinary double figure numbers.
behaviors: `close` with no arguments closes the current figure when one exists. If no figure exists, it is a successful no-op that returns `1` without creating a default figure.
`close('all')` closes every open figure. Networking resources use explicit selectors such as `close('clients')` and `close('servers')`.
`close(fig)` closes an explicit figure handle and raises a figure-handle diagnostic if that explicit handle does not exist.
`close(t)` closes the TCP client struct `t` that was previously returned by `tcpclient` or `accept`. Subsequent socket operations on that client raise MATLAB-style “not connected” diagnostics.
`close(s)` closes the TCP server struct `s` that was returned by `tcpserver`. Any clients that were accepted from that server are also disconnected to match MATLAB’s lifecycle rules.

`close('clients')` closes every registered TCP client (including those produced by `accept`). Likewise, `close('servers')` closes every TCP server. Use those explicit networking selectors instead of `close('all')`, which is reserved for figure closure.

Plotting forms return scalar double `1` after a successful or no-op close. A `0` status is reserved for refused closure, which RunMat cannot yet produce because `CloseRequestFcn` callbacks are not implemented. Networking inputs return `1` when at least one resource was closed and `0` otherwise.
Invalid arguments raise `RunMat:close:InvalidArgument`. Structs that do not contain the hidden RunMat networking identifiers raise `RunMat:close:InvalidHandle`.
Networking happens on the CPU. Resident numeric arguments are not networking resources and are rejected as non-host figure targets before provider dispatch.

In RunMat mode, networking resources may be passed as separate arguments or wrapped in nested cell arrays, and networking selectors may be scalar strings. Separate variadic targets are rejected in compatibility mode; plotting figure targets are not accepted through cell containers in the current implementation.

In RunMat mode, scalar and array figure numbers can use any of the eight integer classes. Values are read exactly, must be positive, and must fit RunMat's `uint32` figure-number range. Compatibility mode rejects typed integer figure numbers because the public compatibility contract does not advertise integer classes.

faqs.question: Is bare `close` safe when no figures are open?
faqs.answer: Yes. RunMat treats bare `close` as a successful no-op when there is no current figure, returning `1` without creating a default figure or raising an invalid-handle error.

faqs.question: What does the return value represent?
faqs.answer: Figure forms return scalar double `1` when the requested operation succeeds or has nothing to close. MATLAB can return `0` when a close callback refuses the request; RunMat does not yet implement that callback path. Networking resources return `1` when at least one client or server was closed and `0` otherwise.

faqs.question: Can I pass multiple clients or servers at once?
faqs.answer: Yes in RunMat mode. Pass them as separate arguments (`close(client1, client2)`) or wrap them in a cell array. Separate variadic targets are a RunMat extension; compatibility mode accepts one target argument.

faqs.question: Does closing a server also close accepted clients?
faqs.answer: Yes. RunMat mirrors MATLAB by closing every client that originated from the server before releasing the listener itself.

faqs.question: What happens if I pass a non-network struct?
faqs.answer: The builtin raises `RunMat:close:InvalidHandle`. Only structs produced by the RunMat networking builtins (`tcpclient`, `tcpserver`, `accept`) carry the hidden identifiers that `close` recognises.

faqs.question: Do GPU arrays require special handling?
faqs.answer: Resident numeric values are not networking resources and are rejected as non-host figure targets before provider access. Networking structs and plotting state remain host-resident.

faqs.question: Is it safe to call close twice?
faqs.answer: It depends on the target. Repeating an explicit figure-number close raises the missing-handle diagnostic, while bare `close` with no current figure is a successful no-op returning `1`. Repeating a networking close returns `0` when no resource remained to close.

faqs.question: Can figure numbers use integer classes?
faqs.answer: Yes in RunMat mode. All eight signed and unsigned integer classes are accepted exactly as host structural selectors within the positive `uint32` range. Compatibility mode requires an ordinary double figure number.

gpu_behavior: `close` performs only CPU-side bookkeeping. Resident numeric values cannot be networking resources and bypass the networking gather path; plotting then rejects them as non-host figure targets without provider dispatch.
